datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: HiRISE image PSP_001513_1655_RED (Home Plate and vicinity)
datasets.measurement_observable: Surface morphology/context imaging used to map Home Plate and silica-rich features
datasets.location_coverage: Home Plate and vicinity, Gusev crater; labeled silica-rich outcrops/soils and other features in Figure 1
datasets.how_used: Provided orbital context and mapping base for distribution of silica-rich outcrops/soils around Home Plate (Figure 1) and for locating/relating surface targets.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mini-TES spectra used to validate/assess mirror-dust correction using surface dust references
datasets.measurement_observable: Thermal infrared radiance/emissivity spectra (including mirror-dust contamination and correction behavior)
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: ~340–2000 cm^-1 (~5–29 µm); more usable range ~360–1800 cm^-1 (as stated)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Sol 78 and Sol 588 (surface dust observations used as reference for correction assessment)
datasets.location_coverage: Surface dust at rim of Bonneville crater (sol 78) and thick surface dust at top of Husband Hill (sol 588)
datasets.spatial_resolution: Nominal Mini-TES spatial resolution 20 mrad (as stated)
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Calibrated to emissivity; mirror-dust correction applied (as described in Section 3.1.1)
datasets.pds_identifiers: Sol 78 sequence ID P3654; Sol 588 sequence ID P3131
datasets.how_used: Compared pre- and post-mirror-contamination dust spectra to assess accuracy of the mirror-dust correction and identify residual misfit across wavenumber ranges (Figure 2a).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mini-TES repeat observations of rock target Buoy to demonstrate precision of mirror-dust correction
datasets.measurement_observable: Thermal infrared emissivity spectra under different temperature conditions relative to mirror dust
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Two observations separated by 25 sols: Sol 481 and Sol 506
datasets.location_coverage: Husband Hill area; rock target 'Buoy' near Jibsheet Ridge (as described)
datasets.spatial_resolution: Nominal Mini-TES spatial resolution 20 mrad (as stated)
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Calibrated to emissivity; mirror-dust correction applied; one spectrum contrast-reduced by 27% for comparison (as described)
datasets.pds_identifiers: Sol 481 p3422 Buoy; Sol 506 p3463 Buoy
datasets.how_used: Demonstrated reproducibility/precision of the mirror-dust correction by correcting two Buoy spectra acquired under different mirror/scene temperature conditions and comparing corrected results (Figures 2b–2c).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mini-TES spectrum of silica-rich soil target Kenosha Comets in Gertrude Weise trench
datasets.measurement_observable: Thermal infrared emissivity spectrum showing diagnostic opal-A features (after mirror-dust correction)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Sol 1197 (as labeled in Figure 3 inset plot)
datasets.location_coverage: Eastern Valley near Home Plate; Gertrude Weise wheel trench; soil target 'Kenosha Comets'
datasets.spatial_resolution: Nominal Mini-TES spatial resolution 20 mrad (as stated)
datasets.pds_identifiers: Sol 1197 sequence ID P3054 (Kenosha Comets; uncorrected/corrected spectrum shown)
datasets.how_used: Used as the purest Mini-TES spectrum of silica-rich material to identify opal-A (including diagnostic ~475 cm^-1 feature) and evaluate viewing-angle/scattering effects in silica-rich soils (Figure 3; Sections 3.1.1–3.1.4).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mini-TES spectra of silica-rich nodular outcrop Clara Zaph4 and adjacent background soil used for soil-component removal
datasets.measurement_observable: Thermal infrared radiance/emissivity spectra; mixed outcrop+soil scene and adjacent soil spectrum used for radiance-domain subtraction
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Sol 1168 (Clara Zaph4 and Clara Zaph background)
datasets.location_coverage: Eastern Valley near Home Plate; silica-rich nodular outcrop target 'Clara Zaph4' and adjacent dusty soil target 'Clara Zaph background' (Figure 7)
datasets.spatial_resolution: Nominal Mini-TES spatial resolution 20 mrad; FOV described as 20 mrad (FWHM 17.5 mrad) in correction discussion
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Calibrated to emissivity; mirror-dust corrected; soil component removed in radiance domain using estimated areal fractions (Section 3.1.5)
datasets.pds_identifiers: Sol 1168 sequence ID P3968 (Clara Zaph4); Sol 1168 sequence ID P3969 (Clara Zaph background)
datasets.how_used: Derived a background-corrected outcrop spectrum to better isolate opaline silica spectral features in the nodular outcrop and assess the influence of contamination and viewing geometry (Figures 7–8; Sections 3.1.5–3.1.6).

datasets.spatial_resolution: Nominal Mini-TES spatial resolution 20 mrad (as stated)
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Calibrated to emissivity; mirror-dust effects discussed; spectra interpreted using low-wavenumber diagnostic feature least affected by dust/contaminants
datasets.pds_identifiers: Raster (7,3) sol 775 P3943; Tyrone Nodules sol 1101 P3842; Tyrone Nodules sol 1102 P3842; Kobal sol 1116 P3857; Clara Zaph1 sol 1152 P3945; Clara Zaph2 sol 1152 P3946; Clara Zaph3 sol 1152 P3947; Clara Zaph4 sol 1152 P3968 (as listed in Figure 9); Philomena Zale sol 1183 P3984; Foreground sur. datasets.how_used: Compared a suite of silica-bearing Mini-TES spectra to characterize variability, contaminant effects (dust/soil), and to support identification of opaline silica in nodular outcrops using the diagnostic ~475 cm^-1 emissivity minimum (Figure 9; Section 3.1.5).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Pancam multispectral observations used to derive/ map the 'hydration signature' for silica-rich targets
datasets.measurement_observable: Visible/near-IR reflectance (Lambert albedo R*) spectra and derived spectral parameters indicating hydration signature near ~1000 nm
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: 432–1009 nm through 13 filters (as stated); key criterion uses 934–1009 nm slope and related slopes
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Examples explicitly used include sols 1158, 1174, and 1198 (as cited in Figure 14); additional supporting context images include sol 1198 true color of Kenosha Comets target (Figure 3)
datasets.location_coverage: Eastern Valley near Home Plate; Clara Zaph4/Elizabeth Mahon area and Gertrude Weise trench area
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Processed approximate true color / false color products from Pancam website; hydration signature computed from four spectral slope parameters (as described in Section 3.2.2)
datasets.pds_identifiers: Sol 1174 Pancam sequence P2588 (Clara Zaph4 multispectral used for hydration signature mapping and spectra); Sol 1158 Pancam sequence P2581 (Gertrude Weise soil spectrum source as cited in Figure 14d); Sol 1198 Pancam sequence P2539 (Kenosha Comets context image in Figure 3)
datasets.how_used: Computed and mapped a Pancam-based hydration signature (including downturn from 934 to 1009 nm) to help identify and spatially map silica-rich/hydrated materials on nodular outcrops and silica-rich soils, and to compare with surface dust spectra (Section 3.2.2; Figure 14).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: APXS in situ elemental chemistry measurements of silica-rich materials near Home Plate (and Calibration Soil reference)
datasets.measurement_observable: Elemental abundances (Na to Y) reported as oxide wt% and trace elements for rocks/soils; used to quantify SiO2 enrichment and contamination/soil subtraction
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Sols 770, 1157, 1179, 1190, 1199, 1225, 1230, 1251, 1288 (as listed in Table 2 and text); plus Stapledon measurement reported for sol 1788 campaign
datasets.location_coverage: Eastern Valley and Home Plate vicinity targets including Kenosha Comets, Lefty Ganote, Nancy Warren, Elizabeth Mahon, Good Question, Innocent Bystander, Norma Luker, Fuzzy Smith; Calibration Soil near Nancy Warren (sol 1230)
datasets.spatial_resolution: Effective APXS FOV circular spot ~25 mm diameter (as stated)
datasets.pds_identifiers: Target/sol references explicitly used in this paper (no APXS observation IDs given): 1190 Kenosha Comets soil; 1199 Lefty Ganote soil; 1225 Nancy Warren outcrop; 1157 Elizabeth Mahon outcrop; 1288 Norma Luker rock; 770 Fuzzy Smith rock; 1251 Innocent Bystander rock; 1179 Good Question outcrop; 1230 Calibration Soil; plus Stapledon (section 4.1.3)
datasets.how_used: Used APXS chemistry (mostly from Ming et al. 2008; Stapledon exception noted) to quantify SiO2 enrichment, compare element ratios to typical soil, and perform linear soil-contamination subtraction using Calibration Soil to estimate corrected compositions (Sections 3.3.1, 4.1; Table 2; Figure 15).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: MIMOS II Mössbauer (MB) spectra-derived iron mineralogy and redox/alteration parameters for silica-rich materials
datasets.measurement_observable: Fe-bearing mineral phases and derived parameters (Fe3+/Fetotal; Mineralogical Alteration Index)
datasets.data_type_product_type: in situ Mössbauer spectra / derived mineralogy
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: MB results reported for multiple Home Plate region silica-rich targets (as summarized in Table 2; derived from Morris et al. 2008)
datasets.location_coverage: Home Plate vicinity targets including Kenosha Comets, Lefty Ganote, Nancy Warren, Elizabeth Mahon, Fuzzy Smith, Innocent Bystander, Good Question (as included in Table 2)
datasets.spatial_resolution: MB beam diameter ~14 mm on sample (as stated)
datasets.pds_identifiers: Target-level references explicitly used (no MB observation IDs given): Kenosha Comets; Lefty Ganote; Nancy Warren; Elizabeth Mahon; Fuzzy Smith; Innocent Bystander; Good Question
datasets.how_used: Used MB-derived mineralogy and derived parameters (Fe3+/Fetotal and MAI) to assess oxidation state/alteration trends of silica-rich materials and evaluate consistency with acid-sulfate leaching vs precipitation hypotheses (Section 3.3.2; Table 2; Discussion Section 5).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Microscopic Imager (MI) images of silica-rich soils/outcrops and related targets used for microtexture interpretation

datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Examples explicitly cited include sols 1101 (Puenta Arenas), 1157 (Elizabeth Mahon), 1189 (Kenosha Comets), 1198 (Lefty Ganote), 1225 (Nancy Warren), 1232 (Darlene Mickelsen), 1251–1252 (Innocent Bystander), 1291 (Norma Luker), 1796 (Stapledon)

queries.query: For Spirit rover operations on Mars in Gusev crater, I need the Mini-TES calibrated, mirror-contamination-corrected products that provide per-observation target temperature information so I can quantify how changing mirror/scene thermal conditions influence retrieved thermal-IR emissivity for repeat stares acquired ~25 sols apart on Husband Hill.

Compile the full set of time-averaged Mini-TES thermal infrared emissivity spectra from the Mars Exploration Rover mission that have been calibrated to emissivity and corrected for pointing-mirror dust effects, to support reproducible comparisons of rock/soil spectral shapes across different observing geometries and thermal environments in Gusev crater.

queries.query: Assemble Spirit rover Mini-TES mirror-dust-corrected thermal-IR emissivity spectra from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater (late mission timeframe) to quantify the presence and variability of opal-A diagnostic bands in silica-enriched soils and nearby nodular outcrops.

Gather Spirit rover Mini-TES raw (EDR-level) thermal-IR measurements from Gusev crater during the Home Plate campaign interval (late mission timeframe) to independently re-derive calibrated emissivity spectra and evaluate the impact of mirror-dust and viewing-geometry effects on silica-bearing surface targets.

output_parsed.paper_title: Characteristics, distribution, origin, and significance of opaline silica observed by the Spirit rover in Gusev crater, Mars

queries.query: Use Spirit rover Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer derived emissivity spectra from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater (around sol 1168) to isolate opaline-silica diagnostic thermal-IR features in silica-rich nodular outcrops by comparing the outcrop scene against an adjacent dusty soil background after mirror-dust correction.

Reprocess Spirit rover Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer reduced radiance spectra from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater (around sol 1168) to perform radiance-domain unmixing/subtraction of an adjacent dusty-soil spectrum from a mixed outcrop+soil scene, quantifying how soil contamination and viewing geometry affect retrieved silica spectral signatures.

queries.query: Calibrated thermal-infrared emissivity spectra from the MER Spirit Mini-TES instrument acquired in the Gusev crater Home Plate vicinity (including Eastern Valley/Tyrone), focusing on early-to-mid mission observations prior to major optics dust accumulation and using the low-wavenumber emissivity minimum near ~475 cm^-1 to identify opaline silica in nodular outcrops.

MER Spirit Mini-TES per-observation target-temperature products associated with calibrated, mirror-dust-corrected emissivity processing for Mars surface spectra in Gusev crater, suitable for screening scene–instrument thermal contrast and selecting observations under stable pre-dust-buildup conditions for silica feature analysis.

output_parsed.paper_title: Characteristics, distribution, origin, and significance of opaline silica observed by the Spirit rover in Gusev crater, Mars

queries.query: For Spirit rover Pancam 13-filter multispectral observations of the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater (mid-mission timeframe), compute Lambert-albedo (radiance factor) spectral slopes emphasizing the 934–1009 nm downturn and related visible–near-IR slopes to generate a hydration-signature map for discriminating silica-rich/hydrated materials from typical dust and basaltic soils.

Using Spirit rover Pancam derived color mosaics of the Home Plate/Eastern Valley region, quantify spatial patterns in approximate true-color and false-color composites to map the geomorphic distribution of light-toned nodular outcrops and disturbed soils associated with hydrated/silica-rich materials, and to assess dust-contamination effects on apparent color at outcrop versus soil scales.

output_parsed.paper_title: Characteristics, distribution, origin, and significance of opaline silica observed by the Spirit rover in Gusev crater, Mars

queries.query: Use Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer science-mode measurements from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater to compute oxide wt% and trace-element abundances for silica-enriched rocks and disturbed light-toned soils, and quantify SiO2 enrichment after subtracting a nearby undisturbed regolith reference.

For Spirit rover Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer observations in the Home Plate region of Gusev crater, analyze the raw/operations records to validate acquisition conditions (e.g., instrument status and measurement geometry) supporting in situ elemental chemistry comparisons between silica-rich targets and a local calibration soil reference.

output_parsed.paper_title: Characteristics, distribution, origin, and significance of opaline silica observed by the Spirit rover in Gusev crater, Mars

queries.query: Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Microscopic Imager close-up images (≈30 µm/pixel) acquired in Gusev crater near Home Plate during roughly sols 1100–1300, targeting silica-rich soils and nodular outcrops to quantify pore-scale texture (microporosity), clast vs. matrix-supported fabrics, and wind-driven sand/dust infill relevant to distinguishing sinter precipitation from leaching.

Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Microscopic Imager images from the Home Plate vicinity acquired during later rover operations (roughly sols 1750–1800) to compare disturbed versus undisturbed silica-rich nodular outcrop surfaces, evaluate brecciation and cementation textures, and assess the extent of aeolian contamination affecting microtexture interpretation.

final_output.query: Find the single Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE red-band observation that images the Home Plate locality within Gusev crater, used as an orbital geomorphic context base for mapping silica-related surface features; return the corresponding reduced data record image product.

Using the same Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE red-band context observation of the Home Plate region in Gusev crater, identify the parent HiRISE reduced-data-record (RDR) dataset that archives this class of map-projected red-channel products for regional context analysis.

Calibrated Mini-TES radiance spectra from the Spirit rover in Gusev crater spanning the prime mission, including observations suitable for converting to emissivity and assessing mirror/optics dust contamination effects on thermal-IR spectra.

Raw (uncalibrated) Spirit Mini-TES spectral observations of surface dust targets acquired early in the mission and again after significant mirror dust accumulation, to reproduce the pre/post-contamination comparison and quantify correction residuals in the thermal-IR.

For Spirit rover operations on Mars in Gusev crater, I need the Mini-TES calibrated, mirror-contamination-corrected products that provide per-observation target temperature information so I can quantify how changing mirror/scene thermal conditions influence retrieved thermal-IR emissivity for repeat stares acquired ~25 sols apart on Husband Hill.

Compile the full set of time-averaged Mini-TES thermal infrared emissivity spectra from the Mars Exploration Rover mission that have been calibrated to emissivity and corrected for pointing-mirror dust effects, to support reproducible comparisons of rock/soil spectral shapes across different observing geometries and thermal environments in Gusev crater.

Assemble Spirit rover Mini-TES mirror-dust-corrected thermal-IR emissivity spectra from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater (late mission timeframe) to quantify the presence and variability of opal-A diagnostic bands in silica-enriched soils and nearby nodular outcrops.

Gather Spirit rover Mini-TES raw (EDR-level) thermal-IR measurements from Gusev crater during the Home Plate campaign interval (late mission timeframe) to independently re-derive calibrated emissivity spectra and evaluate the impact of mirror-dust and viewing-geometry effects on silica-bearing surface targets.

Use Spirit rover Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer derived emissivity spectra from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater (around sol 1168) to isolate opaline-silica diagnostic thermal-IR features in silica-rich nodular outcrops by comparing the outcrop scene against an adjacent dusty soil background after mirror-dust correction.

Reprocess Spirit rover Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer reduced radiance spectra from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater (around sol 1168) to perform radiance-domain unmixing/subtraction of an adjacent dusty-soil spectrum from a mixed outcrop+soil scene, quantifying how soil contamination and viewing geometry affect retrieved silica spectral signatures.

Calibrated thermal-infrared emissivity spectra from the MER Spirit Mini-TES instrument acquired in the Gusev crater Home Plate vicinity (including Eastern Valley/Tyrone), focusing on early-to-mid mission observations prior to major optics dust accumulation and using the low-wavenumber emissivity minimum near ~475 cm^-1 to identify opaline silica in nodular outcrops.

MER Spirit Mini-TES per-observation target-temperature products associated with calibrated, mirror-dust-corrected emissivity processing for Mars surface spectra in Gusev crater, suitable for screening scene–instrument thermal contrast and selecting observations under stable pre-dust-buildup conditions for silica feature analysis.

For Spirit rover Pancam 13-filter multispectral observations of the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater (mid-mission timeframe), compute Lambert-albedo (radiance factor) spectral slopes emphasizing the 934–1009 nm downturn and related visible–near-IR slopes to generate a hydration-signature map for discriminating silica-rich/hydrated materials from typical dust and basaltic soils.

Using Spirit rover Pancam derived color mosaics of the Home Plate/Eastern Valley region, quantify spatial patterns in approximate true-color and false-color composites to map the geomorphic distribution of light-toned nodular outcrops and disturbed soils associated with hydrated/silica-rich materials, and to assess dust-contamination effects on apparent color at outcrop versus soil scales.

Use Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer science-mode measurements from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater to compute oxide wt% and trace-element abundances for silica-enriched rocks and disturbed light-toned soils, and quantify SiO2 enrichment after subtracting a nearby undisturbed regolith reference.

For Spirit rover Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer observations in the Home Plate region of Gusev crater, analyze the raw/operations records to validate acquisition conditions (e.g., instrument status and measurement geometry) supporting in situ elemental chemistry comparisons between silica-rich targets and a local calibration soil reference.

For the Mars Exploration Rover Spirit MIMOS II Mössbauer investigation, assemble the iron-mineral phase abundances and derived oxidation/alteration metrics for silica-enriched soils and nodular outcrops in the Gusev crater Home Plate vicinity to quantify Fe3+/Fe_total and alteration intensity.

Retrieve the processed Mössbauer summary spectra acquired by the Spirit rover on silica-rich soils and outcrops in the Home Plate vicinity of Gusev crater to enable independent spectral refitting of Fe-bearing phases and validation of redox/alteration parameters.

Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Microscopic Imager close-up images (≈30 µm/pixel) acquired in Gusev crater near Home Plate during roughly sols 1100–1300, targeting silica-rich soils and nodular outcrops to quantify pore-scale texture (microporosity), clast vs. matrix-supported fabrics, and wind-driven sand/dust infill relevant to distinguishing sinter precipitation from leaching.

Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Microscopic Imager images from the Home Plate vicinity acquired during later rover operations (roughly sols 1750–1800) to compare disturbed versus undisturbed silica-rich nodular outcrop surfaces, evaluate brecciation and cementation textures, and assess the extent of aeolian contamination affecting microtexture interpretation.
